subject: maths
title: Application of derivatives: rates and the best box
instruction: Work through the chapter one step at a time.

activity.instruction: Predict first, then watch. After that, solve the challenges with the sliders.
activity.intro: A circular rangoli grows outwards at a steady speed. How fast does its area grow?
activity.picture:
<svg viewBox="0 0 400 330" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="400" height="330" rx="14" fill="#FFFDF7"/>
<circle cx="200" cy="165" r="{r*7}" fill="#F3A328" opacity=".35" stroke="#E96E24" stroke-width="4"/>
<circle cx="200" cy="165" r="{r*5}" fill="none" stroke="#CC3054" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="8 6"/>
<circle cx="200" cy="165" r="{r*2.5}" fill="#FBD064" stroke="#631654" stroke-width="3"/>
<line x1="200" y1="165" x2="{200+r*7}" y2="165" stroke="#3D0E37" stroke-width="3"/>

<text x="16" y="30" font-size="20" font-weight="800" fill="#631654">r = {r} cm</text>
<text x="16" y="56" font-size="18" fill="#242430">Area = {A:1} cm²</text>
<text x="384" y="30" font-size="20" font-weight="800" text-anchor="end" fill="#CC3054">dA/dt = {dAdt:1} cm²/s</text>
<text x="384" y="316" font-size="15" text-anchor="end" fill="#6E6170">the edge moves {k} cm every second</text></svg>

solution.title: Worked solution
solution.note: The edge moves at the same speed, but a bigger circle adds more area every second.

predict.text: The radius is {r} cm. If the radius doubles to 10 cm, the area will become…
predict.explain: Area went from 78.5 to {A:1} cm². A = πr², so doubling r makes the area 2² = 4 times as big.

predict.text: The edge speed stays at 2 cm/s. At r = 10 cm, will the area grow faster or slower than at r = 5 cm?
predict.explain: dA/dt went from 62.8 to {dAdt:1} cm²/s. dA/dt = 2πr × dr/dt grows with r.

goals.text: Make the area grow at 40π ≈ 125.7 cm²/s.
goals.say: 40 pi. For example radius 10 at 2 centimetres per second, or radius 5 at 4.

goals.text: With dr/dt = 3 cm/s, find the radius where the area grows at 60π ≈ 188.5 cm²/s.
goals.say: Radius 10. Two pi times 10 times 3 is 60 pi.

activity.doneText: You can find rates of change!

activity.instruction: Predict first, then find the corner cut that gives the biggest box.

solution.title: Worked solution
lines: dV/dx = 0 when x = 8, so the biggest box is 8 × 32² = 8192 cm³
solution.note: Before x = 8, dV/dx is positive (volume rising). After it, dV/dx is negative (volume falling).

predict.text: The cut goes from 2 cm to 6 cm. The volume will…
predict.explain: It rose from 3872 to {V:0} cm³. The box gets taller faster than its base shrinks.

predict.text: Now the cut goes from 8 cm to 16 cm. Will the box keep getting bigger?
predict.explain: It fell from 8192 to {V:0} cm³. The base shrinks so much that height can't make up for it. The maximum is in between.

goals.text: Find the cut that gives the biggest possible box.
goals.say: 8 centimetres. The box holds 8192 cubic centimetres, and dV by dx is zero there.

goals.text: Make a box that holds exactly 6912 cm³.

activity.doneText: You found the maximum with calculus!

activity.instruction: Move each function into the right group for the interval shown.
activity.intro: If the derivative is positive, the function is increasing. If it is negative, the function is decreasing.

items.say: The derivative 2x is positive when x is positive.
The derivative 2x is negative when x is negative.
The derivative of e to the x is e to the x, always positive.
The derivative minus 1 over x squared is always negative.
The derivative is minus 3, so it always decreases.
3x squared is never negative, so x cubed keeps increasing.
The derivative 1 over x is positive for positive x.
The derivative minus sin x is negative between 0 and pi.

activity.doneText: You read the sign of the derivative!

activity.instruction: Put the steps for a maximum or minimum problem in order.
activity.intro: Every maximum and minimum problem follows the same steps.

items.say: First, write what you want to make biggest or smallest as a function of one variable.
Solve to find the critical points.
Negative second derivative means a maximum, positive means a minimum.
Finally, work out the value and give its unit.

activity.instruction: Tap the best answer. Read why after each question.
activity.intro: Time for a quick quiz on this chapter.

questions.q: The radius of a circle grows at 3 cm/s. How fast is the area growing when r = 10 cm?
The side of a cube grows at 2 cm/s. How fast is its volume growing when the side is 5 cm?
questions.explain: V = s³, so dV/dt = 3s² × ds/dt = 3 × 25 × 2 = 150 cm³/s.

questions.q: What is the slope of the tangent to y = x² at x = 3?
For f(x) = x³ − 3x, where is the local maximum?
questions.explain: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 gives x = ±1. f″(x) = 6x is −6 at x = −1, which is negative, so that is a maximum.

questions.q: If f′(c) = 0, then f always has a maximum or a minimum at c.
questions.explain: Not always. For f(x) = x³, f′(0) = 0, but the curve keeps rising through x = 0. It is a point of inflection.

questions.q: Two positive numbers add up to 20. What is the largest their product can be?
questions.explain: Product P = x(20 − x). P′ = 20 − 2x = 0 at x = 10, so the numbers are 10 and 10 and P = 100.

questions.assertion: f(x) = x² is decreasing for x < 0.
questions.explain: Both are true, and a negative derivative is exactly why the function decreases there.
f′(x) = eˣ is positive for every x.
